subject: QBR dry-run: launch triage, mitigation ledger & ownership asks
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sara.jones@acme.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: QBR dry-run: launch triage, mitigation ledger & ownership asks

Team —

Ahead of tomorrow's QBR dry-run (09/08 11:00 PT) I ran a pass through the roadmap slices that are still at risk and pulled a mitigation ledger (attached). Short summary and asks below — please read the ledger tabbed by feature and update ownership cells before EOD Pacific.

Top concerns (product + eng):
- Model-on-hosting migrations: two models still have performance regressions at 4k tokens under load (seen in pre-prod). Impact: X% latency SLO burn and potential canary rollback.
- Canary rollout window for the new cache warm-up: currently scheduled for 48h; ops recommends extending to 72h given burst-scaling tests.
- Billing rounding bug in usage ingestion that affects reserved capacity accounting for Dedicated customers (estimating ~2-3% invoice variance).

Immediate asks (owners + deadlines):
- @markus_klein: update the model mitigation plan in the ledger with exact rollback criteria and a dry-run checklist (due: 09/07 23:59 PT).
- @grace_oconnor: confirm canary window recommendation and add the guardrail for auto-fallback to the Gate Criteria matrix (attached) — due: 09/07 23:00 PT.
- Engineering leads: annotate the ledger with estimated QA cycles and SLO exposure per feature (use the SLO column).

External note for Acme: Sara — the attached agenda includes a short slot to walk through the contingency for the model migration. We'll keep the customer-facing runway conservative and communicate the rollback policy during the QBR dry-run.

Attachments: qbr-dryrun-agenda.pdf (3 pages), mitigation_ledger_v2.xlsx (tabs: overview, ledger_by_feature, owners), gate-criteria-matrix.csv

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sara.jones@acme.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 18:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QBR dry-run: launch triage, mitigation ledger & ownership asks

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 3:04 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Ahead of tomorrow's QBR dry-run (09/08 11:00 PT) I ran a pass through the roadmap slices that are still at risk and pulled a mitigation ledger (attached). Short summary and asks below — please read the ledger tabbed by feature and update ownership cells before EOD Pacific.

Thanks Kim — quick updates from engineering side:

- Performance regressions: engineering confirmed the 4k token regressions are tied to a fused attention kernel mismatch introduced in the last compilation pass. We have a patch candidate that reduces median latency by ~12% in the pre-prod harness but we need two more stress runs against the live batching service to be confident. I put the patch into a 'dry-run' branch.
- Rollback criteria: proposing these two thresholds — (1) 99th pctl latency increase > 25% vs baseline for > 10m, or (2) error rate > 0.5% sustained for > 5m. If either triggers, immediate rollback to the previous model variant and alert the CS lead.

I updated the mitigation_ledger_v2.xlsx (ledger_by_feature tab) with the patch branch and stress-test owners. I also added a short TODO for product to confirm acceptable rollback SLA to communicate to the customer.

One request: can we get a small table of token mix for Acme's top workload (prompt length distribution) so we can simulate realistic batching? Sara, if you can share last 72h ingest characteristics that would help — or we can run a representative replay with anonymized traces.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sara.jones@acme.com, partners@cloudintegrate.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 20:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QBR dry-run: launch triage, mitigation ledger & ownership asks

Thanks — I reviewed the ledger. A few discrete notes: 

- Canary window: agree to extend to 72h for the cache warm-up. I'll add an explicit metric: sustained QPS at 85th percentile for 3 consecutive 15-minute intervals as a green-check for progressing from canary->ramp.
- Billing rounding bug: finance flagged a 2.2% variance in our reserved capacity calculation on a reproducible ingest pattern. I'll loop in finance and create an action (we should not ship this to Dedicated customers without a fixed patch).
- Comms plan: Kimberly, please include the two rollback thresholds Markus proposed in the dry-run script. We should also be explicit about the customer-facing phrasing: "graceful fallback to verified model variant while we complete a hotfix."

I updated gate-criteria-matrix.csv with the canary metric and put a short note in the agenda slot: who speaks, and what the customer will hear.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sara.jones@acme.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 02:17:00 +0000
Subject: Re: QBR dry-run: launch triage, mitigation ledger & ownership asks

Received and thanks both. Quick recap of owners / deliverables before the 11:00 PT dry-run: 

- Markus: finalize stress-run results and formalize rollback thresholds in the ledger (due: 09/07 23:59 PT — noted as complete).
- Grace: publish canary metric in gate matrix and confirm the extended window with Ops (due: 09/07 23:00 PT — noted as complete).
- Kim (me): I'll lead the customer-facing contingency slide and run the dry script (11:00 PT).
- Ops: be ready to hold the first 72h canary and to execute auto-fallback if thresholds breach.
- Finance: holding on Dedicated shipments until billing bug is fixed; I'll coordinate a separate escalation if we cannot land a patch before QBR.

Sara — we'll keep Acme in the loop during the dry-run. If anything material changes, we'll follow up after the session with a short note and an updated action tracker.

See you in the room.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference
